challenges.says: The second open question treats a typed minus sign as possibly setting the smallest value, but hexadecimal parsing rejects a sign with a format error that is silently ignored, so the value stays unchanged; the Minimum branch (EditPolNumericData.vb:47-48) is only reached on overflow, which a leading minus cannot cause, so the question misstates the current behaviour.

The first open question asks about capitals and no prefix, but the code fixes this (String.Format "{0:X}", line 26) as a fact, not an open point, and criterion 1 does not state it; either state it in the criterion or drop the question.

The second criterion (ordinary behaviour when hexadecimal mode is off) cites layer-web and base.decision-25 (messages, forms and queries), which say nothing about the field falling back to the standard control; the citation does not support the criterion.

Criterion 4 and the rule leave out that empty text leaves the value unchanged and that text too large for the 32-bit field in a 32-bit value is clamped to that smaller maximum; the story only hints at this in the term, so the 32-bit versus 64-bit clamp is not testable from the criteria.
